statement_en: Let $a_n:=(-1)^n$. Then its partial sums are $$S_n:=\begin{cases}1&n\text{ is even}\\0&n\text{ is odd}\end{cases}$$ so $S_n$ does not converge. However, this sequence is Cesaro summable, because $$\sigma_N:=\frac{S_0+\cdots+S_{N-1}}{N}=\frac{\lfloor\frac{N}{2}+1\rfloor}{N}$$ and its limit is $\frac{1}{2}$.
